verdict.rationale: Square's OAuth API and access tokens are explicitly scope-controlled ('authorize only the scopes your application needs'), and this same granular-permission model is used by the remote MCP server's OAuth login, confirmed live via a probe showing the MCP endpoint is OAuth-gated with a documented authorization server. The local MCP server also supports a DISALLOW_WRITES=true env flag for read-only least-privilege restriction. missing for 10: independent/third-party confirmation of scope granularity in practice (e.g. a developer walkthrough enumerating exact scope list) and hands-on evidence of an agent successfully using a narrowly-scoped token end-to-end.
